headline: Your Swell waterfall journey.
subheadline: A scrollable GTMx strategy artifact for routing DSOs, MSOs, and multi-location specialty groups into the right Swell reputation, patient-experience, and employee-feedback offer. List building, campaign angles, and sample copy, prepared for Dean Despain.
productSummary: Swell (swellcx.com — not swell.com water bottles, not swell.is ecommerce) is an AI-powered healthcare reputation management and patient experience platform for multi-location healthcare groups. Homepage: from generating more reviews and monitoring ratings to automating patient, provider, and employee feedback, Swell gives multi-location groups centralized operational visibility across every location, brand, and provider in one AI-powered platform. Core products on swellcx.com: Online Reputation Management (ORM) — automated review invites plus AI-drafted on-brand HIPAA-compliant responses for one-click approval across Google, Healthgrades, and Facebook; Patient Experience Insights (PXI) — post-visit surveys, NPS and CSAT, comment clustering by location and provider; Employee Experience Insights (EXI) — anonymous pulse surveys, eNPS, Glassdoor/Indeed monitoring; Healthcare Listings Management across 200+ directories; Ticketing and workflow automation. The Swell agent reads every review and survey, drafts responses, clusters themes, detects rating/NPS drops, flags integration failures, and routes high-risk feedback (safety, billing, HIPAA) to the right manager. Built for DSOs, MSOs, and PE-backed specialty groups from 5 to 500+ locations with native region / brand / clinic / provider hierarchies. Integrations named on-site: Dentrix, Open Dental, Ortho2 Edge, athenahealth, eClinicalWorks, NexHealth, Sikka, Dental Intelligence, Ortho2 Edge, Denticon, Zenoti, Cloud9, and 100+ EHR/PMS systems; Google review API partner. HIPAA compliant and SOC 2 Type II certified, U.S.-based healthcare-grade infrastructure; most groups live in days, not months. Homepage proof: 5X more reviews, 1,000% more responses, 4.92 average rating. Product pages: 5× more reviews, 5× more review responses, 4.92 average star rating across 12,000+ locations. Official AI page (updated 2026-06-18): more than 12,000 healthcare practices served; founded 2016; HQ Holladay, Utah; CEO Zeke Kuch. Named case studies on swellcx.com: Next Level Urgent Care (1,552% increase in monthly review volume; 1,640 reviews in the first 4 months); Sierra Neurosurgery Group (1,311% increase; 4.92 average Google rating; 24% invite-to-review conversion; Helen Bolstad, Marketing Director: “Swell is heads and shoulders above our prior vendor”); Smile Doctors (222% increase; 36,000+ NPS surveys; 500+ locations; 9% invite-to-review; Ansley Taylor); Utah Orthopaedic Specialists (10% increase in average review score; 15% invite-to-review). One large DSO on the ORM page sees 20 reviews per location per month and 3× the review volume of its previous platform. Competitors named for comparison on swellcx.com: Birdeye, Podium, Rater8, Reputation.com, SocialClimb. Buyers named on-site: COOs, CMOs, CFOs, regional ops directors, marketing leaders, HR leaders, and PE operating partners. Specialties named: dental, dermatology, orthodontics, ophthalmology/vision, pediatrics, urgent care, med spa, plastic surgery, behavioral health, pain management, veterinary, neurosurgery, orthopedic, multi-specialty. Employee count is not published on swellcx.com.
coreInsight: Dean already sells a healthcare-native AI agent so DSOs, MSOs, and specialty groups stop chasing reviews, surveys, and listings by hand across every clinic. The one list is multi-location healthcare groups (DSOs, MSOs, PE-backed specialty networks) — not restaurants, retail, or multi-industry local business. The one routing signal is reputation_stack_state: how reviews, listings, and patient-experience language already show up publicly, because BuiltWith plus a Google Business Profile scrape plus a homepage scrape returns a named generalist reputation tool (Birdeye, Podium, Rater8, Reputation.com, SocialClimb), live multi-location listings with unanswered or thin reviews, PX/NPS language with no named competitor, or none of those, in one pull. Specialty labels (dental vs derm vs vet) are merge tags after the account is routed. They are not a second waterfall. TAM size is not published on swellcx.com — 12,000+ is locations already on Swell, not the market.

sections.label: Signal
sections.title: The signal is how reviews and PX already show up on their stack
sections.takeaway: BuiltWith plus a Google Business Profile scrape plus a homepage scrape already names a generalist reputation tool, live multi-location listings with unanswered or thin reviews, PX/NPS language with no named competitor, or none of those. That stack-state is stronger than a title guess, and it is cheap to collect.

sections.label: Waterfall
sections.title: One cascade routes every DSO, MSO, and specialty group
sections.takeaway: First match wins. Named Birdeye / Podium / Rater8 / Reputation.com / SocialClimb goes first, then multi-location Google listings with unanswered or thin reviews, then PX/NPS language with no named competitor, then every remaining in-TAM multi-location healthcare group.

sections.label: Tiers
sections.title: Each stack-state gets a different first offer
sections.takeaway: Competitor reputation tools get a Healthcare Switch Brief. Unanswered or thin Google listings get a Review Velocity Brief. PX/NPS language with no competitor gets a PX Command Center Brief. The rest get the Multi-Location Reputation Playbook.

sections.label: Campaigns
sections.title: Switch the generalist, fill unanswered listings, unify PX, then cover the rest
sections.takeaway: The list is always in-TAM DSOs, MSOs, and specialty groups, aimed at COOs, CMOs, CFOs, regional ops directors, marketing leaders, HR leaders, and PE operating partners. Specialty is a merge tag, not a second TAM. A/Bs sit on the exclusive routes.

sections.label: Email Copy
sections.title: Copy that names the review or PX state already on their stack
sections.takeaway: Notice the competitor, the unanswered Google reviews, or the NPS page, poke the multi-location gap that stack-state implies, then ask for a one-letter yes.

sections.label: Launch
sections.title: Launch the competitor-switch route first
sections.takeaway: Start where they already pay Birdeye, Podium, or another generalist and still lack healthcare-native rollups, HIPAA drafts, and EHR-triggered invites. Prove reply density, then roll unanswered listings, PX unification, and the remaining-TAM catch-all.

signalReasons: Apollo plus LinkedIn plus DSO/MSO and specialty-group directories plus Google Maps healthcare categories are the TAM Dean already sells into: multi-location healthcare groups (DSOs, MSOs, PE-backed specialty networks). Account-count TAM is not published on swellcx.com — do not invent one. 12,000+ is locations already on Swell.

The same BuiltWith / GBP / homepage scrape returns reputation_stack_state: a named generalist (Birdeye, Podium, Rater8, Reputation.com, SocialClimb — all compared on swellcx.com), live multi-location listings with unanswered or thin reviews, or PX/NPS language with no named competitor, which is enough to route without a second expensive enrichment product.

The ladder maps to live Swell positioning on swellcx.com: purpose-built vs Birdeye/Podium (retail templates, flat accounts), 5× more reviews and a 4.92 rating across 12,000+ locations, native region/brand/clinic/provider rollups, EHR/PMS-triggered invites, and reviews + surveys + employee feedback on one data layer.
Specialty labels (dental, derm, vet, behavioral health) are scrape filters and merge tags. They are not a second waterfall. Apollo is email last after the domain is routed, never the TAM spine alone.

routingRules.why: Already a customer. Named case-study logos on swellcx.com are not enough to exclude every subsidiary or newly acquired clinic.

routingRules.if: in_tam AND reputation_stack_state = competitor_tool (Birdeye, Podium, Rater8, Reputation.com, SocialClimb, or another named generalist reputation / review / survey tool on BuiltWith / site)
routingRules.why: They already pay for review generation. Strongest intent for Swell's purpose-built pitch: swellcx.com/online-reputation contrasts Swell vs Birdeye/Podium (retail templates, flat accounts, compliance bolted on) and cites 5× more reviews and a 4.92 rating across 12,000+ locations.

routingRules.if: in_tam AND reputation_stack_state = listings_unanswered_or_thin (multi-location Google / Healthgrades listings live, reviews unanswered or review volume thin vs peer clinics, no named competitor tool)
routingRules.why: The listings exist; the motion does not. Pain is inferred from the trigger: office managers chasing reviews by hand, a regional ops director who cannot read 8,000 reviews a quarter (homepage), unanswered reviews that stick before a rating drop hits Google.

routingRules.if: in_tam AND reputation_stack_state = px_language_no_competitor (patient-experience / NPS / CSAT / survey language on site, no named competitor, not the unanswered/thin-listing case)
routingRules.why: They already talk PX, but public reviews and private surveys are not on one data layer. Maps to Patient Experience Insights on swellcx.com/patient-experience: a wait-time complaint in a survey can trigger a ticket and explain a rating dip the same week.

routingRules.if: in_tam AND none of the above
routingRules.why: Still in TAM (DSOs, MSOs, specialty groups). Softest CTA around the full platform — ORM + PXI + EXI + listings + ticketing. Mandatory 100% coverage.

One large DSO: 20 reviews per location per month and 3× the review volume of its previous platform.

tiers.accounts: unknown; not published on swellcx.com — keep each tier ≥~1,500 contacts before launch

tiers.name: Tier 2
tiers.label: Multi-location listings, unanswered or thin reviews
tiers.trigger: Google Business Profile / Healthgrades listings live across multiple locations, reviews unanswered or review volume thin vs peer clinics, no named competitor tool
tiers.pain: The clinics are findable; the reviews are not working. Homepage: a regional ops director cannot read 8,000 reviews a quarter and a CMO cannot draft responses for 200 clinics. Unanswered reviews and thin volume sit in local search until a rating drop hits Google.

The agent reads every review, drafts a HIPAA-compliant response, and routes safety/billing/HIPAA mentions as tickets. Homepage: 5X more reviews, 1,000% more responses, 4.92 average rating.
tiers.dataSource: Google Maps / GBP scrape + location count
tiers.replyDensity: High - listings prove they already compete in local search
tiers.share: est. 15-25% (flagged estimate; not published on swellcx.com)

tiers.name: Tier 3
tiers.label: PX / NPS language, no named competitor
tiers.trigger: Site mentions patient experience, NPS, CSAT, patient surveys, or a PX program, with no named competitor tool and not the unanswered/thin-listing case
tiers.pain: They already care about PX, but survey data and public reviews live in separate silos. swellcx.com/patient-experience: generalist tools keep survey data and review data in separate silos; a wait-time complaint and a Google review about the same location never connect.

Surveys after every visit, NPS/CSAT by location and provider, open-ended comments clustered automatically, low scores become tickets. Smile Doctors (on swellcx.com): 222% more monthly reviews, 36,000+ NPS surveys, 500+ locations.

tiers.name: Catch-all
tiers.label: Remaining in-TAM DSO / MSO / specialty groups

tiers.pain: Operators still answer for the numbers without centralized visibility across reviews, surveys, employees, and listings. Homepage: they need to know what is working, where the gaps are, and which locations need attention before a rating drop hits Google.
tiers.valueProp: One AI agent and one data layer across Online Reputation Management, Patient Experience Insights, Employee Experience Insights, Healthcare Listings Management, and Ticketing. HIPAA + SOC 2 Type II. Live in days, not months. Softest CTA.

launchPlan: Confirm in_tam definition: multi-location healthcare groups only — DSOs, MSOs, and PE-backed specialty networks (dental, dermatology, orthodontics, vision, pediatrics, urgent care, med spa, plastic surgery, behavioral health, pain management, veterinary, neurosurgery, orthopedic, multi-specialty). Do not expand into retail, restaurants, or field services. swell.com (water bottles) and swell.is (ecommerce) are different companies — never mix.

Pull Apollo / Sales Nav for those companies, then BuiltWith + Google Business Profile scrape + homepage scrape for reputation_stack_state. Suppress known Swell customers when visible. Named case studies are not a blanket exclude.
Healthcare-vertical TAM size is not published on swellcx.com. Do not invent an account count. Scrape first; do not launch a tier under ~1,500 contacts.
Launch Tier 1 only until reply density is clear (target ~1 positive / 150-300). Competitor detections (Birdeye, Podium, Rater8, Reputation.com, SocialClimb) are the strongest intent.
Add Tier 2 listings_unanswered_or_thin once Tier 1 copy is stable.
Add Tier 3 px_language_no_competitor, then the catch-all for remaining in-TAM accounts.
Enrich emails via Apollo only after the account is routed.
A/B Switch Brief vs Sierra/Next Level proof on Tier 1 before cloning angles downward. Specialty is a merge tag, not a parallel campaign.
